data.title: Calamine lotion
data.summary: XI Miscellaneous · Shake lotion (zinc oxide with a small amount of ferric oxide) — soothing, drying, mildly astringent
data.body:
_Topicals · XI Miscellaneous_

**Class:** Shake lotion (zinc oxide with a small amount of ferric oxide) — soothing, drying, mildly astringent

## Mechanism of action
- Zinc oxide/calamine powder suspended in water: water evaporates → cooling, antipruritic effect
- Powder remains on the skin → drying and protective; mildly astringent and antiseptic
- Ferric oxide gives the pink colour

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acute itchy rashes: varicella, insect bites, miliaria rubra, sunburn, urticaria (symptomatic), mild contact dermatitis
- Weeping lesions (drying)

## Dose & formulations
- Shake well; dab on 2–4 times daily; allow to dry

## Adverse effects
- Dryness with prolonged use; caking on hairy skin
- Phenol-containing versions — avoid in infants and pregnancy

## Contraindications
- Very dry or chronic lichenified eczema (too drying)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe (plain calamine).

## Viva points
- Classic example of a shake lotion (powder + liquid)
- Cooling by evaporation; drying for weeping lesions

_Sources: Khopkar ch.28 (Miscellaneous topical agents); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
